newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: FORECAST-Sri Lanka stocks seen rising further. [corrected 14:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sri Lanka stocks seen rising further. [corrected 14:35 GMT]

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks, which broke the psychological 750-point barrier to close at a 22-month high on Wednesday, will likely breach 800 points by August, analysts said on Thursday.
The all-share index, which closed at 763.5 points on Wednesday, rose further during Thursday's trading.

"The all-share going above 800 points by August is eminently possible, fuelled by good growth expectations in the period to June 1997," said Nandakumar Nair, research director of brokerage John Keells.
Colombo stocks went into a tailspin in 1995 when heavy government borrowing to upgrade its military to fight the Tamil separatist rebels pushed up interest rates.
The Tamil rebels are fighting a 13-year-old war for a separate state in Sri Lanka's north and east.

Rebel attacks on vital economic installations and civilians over the past two years, followed by a crippling drought and power cuts, which hit agriculture and industry, compounded the misery, analysts said.
Gross domestic product (GDP) growth fell to 3.8 percent in 1996 from 5.5 percent in 1995.
But the situation has changed since then. Rains are expected to be normal this year and corporate profits have been higher, leading to a general optimism.
The Central Bank has said it is targeting six percent GDP growth in 1997.
"Results up to June, which is the first quarter for firms with an April/March accounting year and six-months for those with a January/December year, will look stunningly good," said Nair.
"The reasons are two-fold. They (results) will be compared with a period in 1996 which was amazingly bad and of course the macro-economic improvements witnessed so far in 1997."
Easing interest rates due to improved liquidity after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios of commercial banks by three percent helped investor sentiment, analysts said.

"Growth expectations remain the key for the index rising to over 800 points by August. But a low interest rate regime is vital if the upward momentum is to be maintained," said Derendra Abayaratna, executive director of The Unit Trust Management Co.
Analysts say the speed at which Colombo stocks have gained in 1997 took many by surprise. The all share index which began the year at 606.7, has so far risen more than 150 points or 26 percent.
Lehman Brothers said in a recent country report that Sri Lanka stocks have gained 15 percent in dollar terms this year.
Ajit Dias Wanigasekera of Ceylinco Stock Brokers forecast the index will be closer to 800 points by the end of 1997 (corrects forecast from 725 points to 800 points).

"The market rerated itself when it crossed 700 points in April, after which it was going to react to fundamentals," he said. "And once it became clear that corporate results were going to be good, there was nothing that could stop the index from rising."
Analysts say Colombo stocks remain attractive despite recent gains.
"The market, which is trading at 12.6 times 1997 earnings, is attrctive compared to regional markets," said Nair.
